A billion dollars a day and thousands of lives lost from a war with no strategy, no exit plan, and no explanation. I went on Colbert and said what bears repeating: Republicans in Congress need to stand with us and stop this war.

Video

DOGE wasn't fixing Social Security—they were making it harder to get your hard-earned benefits.

We created the Social Security War Room to fight back.
theguardian.com/us-news/2026…

Millions in oil futures traded minutes before Trump's Iran ceasefire.

Then the White House had to remind staff not to trade on insider info.

We need a full investigation. The American people deserve answers.

The Trump administration is starting to give refunds from his illegal tariffs.

Not to the consumers who paid for more expensive goods—only for the corporations that raised their prices on those consumers.

Donald Trump must give the American people their money back.

People can't afford groceries, but Republicans in Congress want taxpayer money for Trump's gold-encrusted ballroom.


FactPost (@factpostnews)

Republicans have introduced legislation to use taxpayer funds to pay for Trump's $400 million ballroom, despite Trump having already secured private funds to cover the ballroom.







— https://nitter.net/factpostnews/status/2049140627628056643#m

Pete Hegseth gutted programs created to reduce civilian harm right after he took office.

Now, thousands of innocent people in Iran are dead from what could have been preventable tragedies.

Hegseth is dangerous. Congress must rein him in and end this war now.

Let's send a firefighter to Congress!

@VoteBobBrooks is going to flip Pennsylvania's 7th District and deliver for working people by fighting for Medicare for All, breaking up corporate monopolies, and taxing the ultra-wealthy.


Bob Brooks (@VoteBobBrooks)

.@ewarren has spent her career taking on the biggest banks, the most powerful corporations, and the politicians who protect them. 

That's the same fight we're waging right here in the Lehigh Valley on behalf of regular people. I'm humbled t

I had the chance to ask RFK Jr. about TrumpRx.

Donald Trump claimed that TrumpRx has reduced drug prices by as much as 600%.

How does that work? Companies pay you to take their drugs?

It’s absurd. I'm not letting them get away with this deception.

Big Tech is building an AI bubble with the same dangerous playbook we saw in 2008.

No rules. No accountability. Plenty of risk for everyone else.

I’m fighting to put guardrails in place—so working families don’t get stuck bailing out reckless CEOs again.

Trump wants to get the Fed to juice the economy in the short run, because it would help him politically, even though it would very much hurt the country in the long run.

Reminder: the Fed is not a political organization that does exactly what the President wants.

Trump promised to lower costs. Instead, his policies have increased the cost of food, housing, child care, and health care.

Trump said he would be a president of peace. Instead, he bombed Iran for reasons he can’t explain.

Americans are paying for Trump’s broken promises.

Amen.


Graham Platner for Senate (@grahamformaine)

People, not private equity firms, should own homes.



— https://nitter.net/grahamformaine/status/2047720195465097590#m

15 million people have lost their health care because of Trump’s and Republicans in Congress’s extreme cuts.

How can there be zero dollars to help those people, but Trump can spend a billion dollars a day bombing Iran?

Americans are selling their plasma to pay for groceries and gas.

Let that sink in.

This is Trump's economy: tax cuts for billionaires, and working people stretching themselves to the brink just to keep the lights on.

Video

United Airlines' CEO is pitching a mega-merger to swallow up American Airlines and create an airline twice the size of its nearest competitor.

That's not competition. It's consolidation—and consumers will pay the price.

I’m pushing back.

bloomberg.com/news/articles/…

The Paramount-Warner Bros. merger is an antitrust nightmare—resulting in a handful of Trump-aligned billionaires controlling huge parts of the media.

State attorneys general are a last line of defense. This fight is not over.


DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm)

Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros has been approved by WBD shareholders.

However, David Zaslav's potential $550M+ pay package for the deal has been rejected.







— https://nitter.net/DiscussingFilm/status/2047319351951282443#m

Tom Perriello is one of the most fearless fighters for working families and I'm proud to endorse him. The insurance industry tried to bully him—he voted to lower costs and expand health care anyway, seat be damned. Zero corporate PAC money. VA needs @tomperriello in Congress.


Tom Perriello (@tomperriello)
